content:
maria: quick sync — follow-up on yesterday's sketch about a tiny local control-plane (we called it the 'splitter') vs routing to regional multipath proxies. trying to capture tradeoffs before i write an RFC.

alex: short version of my stance: prefer splitter (local stub) for auth locality and lower latency, but worry about ops complexity and key material sync. :thinking:

simon: agree with alex on auth. splitter keeps tokens in-customer-vpc which helps compliance. downside: every version bump means a rolling upgrade inside customer VPCs.

chitra: can we avoid heavy upgrades? what if splitter is super-thin (only routing + auth cache) and uses control-plane push for policy? then binary churn is minimal.

maria: that's the idea i had — splitter = static binary, config driven. control plane sends signed policy blobs. splitter validates signature via CP public key, no per-tenant keys required.

alex: signature model seems OK. still concerned about connectivity when CP unreachable — fallback to multipath proxies needed. i.e. splitter primary, multipath proxy fallback.

jess: how does multipath proxy differ from existing regional endpoints? we already have regional relays but not multipath balancing across them.

maria: multipath proxy = edge relay that can open concurrent upstreams to multiple regions and pick fastest/healthy; supports affinity and source-ip preservation. idea is to use it as fallback and for tenants unwilling to deploy splitter.

simon: ops implications: multipath proxy increases egress cost and complexity but centralizes upgrades. splitter pushes complexity to customer side and reduces our egress. tradeoff depends on customer scale.

chitra: we should enumerate failure modes. quick list: CP unreachable, controlplane cert rotation, per-tenant routing mismatch, IP preservation fail, NAT hairpin issues, auth cache staleness.

maria: adding to that — rollout semantics: default = multipath proxy for all new tenants. offer splitter as opt-in for Dedicated/Private customers. allow canary split per-customer via Console flag.

deploy-bot: deploy started: cp/policy-distributor v2 -> canary (10%) — 5601112235

alex: thinking about metrics we need: split ratio, auth-cache-hit, fallback-rate-to-multipath, median-upstream-rtt, preserved-source-ip-rate. Also a per-tenant egress-cost-estimate.

jess: edge-case: what about customers that require egress IP preservation and also strict private peering? splitter can't always preserve IP unless they NAT through their side. we should document recommended network topologies.

maria: agreed. add recommended topologies section in RFC: 1) dedicated splitter with local SNAT in tenant VPC 2) multipath proxy with per-tenant static egress pools 3) HA peering + region affinity for low-latency customers.

chitra: security note: splitter must provide an attestation endpoint so CP can verify it's real during onboarding. attestation can be signed TPM cert or an OIDC exchange with short-lived token.

alex: implementation spike idea: build a minimal splitter PoC that handles: inbound TLS termination from tenant apps, simple HMAC-based token validation (using CP-pushed secret), and upstream multiplex to multipath proxy. 2-week spike.

maria: can we sketch a sample config?

maria: ```
# splitter.yaml
listen: 127.0.0.1:8080
control_plane_pubkey: /etc/redwood/cp.pub
policies_path: /var/lib/redwood/policies.json
upstreams:
  - type: multipath
    endpoints: [region-a.relay.internal, region-b.relay.internal]
fallback_timeout_ms: 200
cache_ttl_s: 60
```

simon: looks good. note: fallback_timeout_ms needs perf benchmarks — too low -> unnecessary fallback, too high -> latency.

alex: test plan: synthetic bench with 99th percentile latency targets, failure injection (CP down), canary on small internal tenant, then invite a customer beta.

maria: next steps: i'll draft RFC with sections: motivation, modes (splitter vs multipath), security model (attestation, signed policies), rollout plan, metrics + observability, cost model, test plan. assign owners for spike: alex (splitter poc), simon (ops cost model), chitra (security attestation), jess (docs/topologies).

jess: assigned, i'll also include sample network diagrams and NAT options. :thumbsup:

maria: sweet. if nobody objects i'll open the RFC tomorrow and tag infra/ops/sec. objections?

alex: none from me. go for it.

simon: no objections.

chitra: go ahead.

maria: thanks — RFC incoming.
